newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JAN 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JAN 30.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The main shareholders of Ceskoslovensko Obchodni Banka met concerning debts of the Slovak collection units (SIJ) which have for a few months not paid installments on a credit of 11 billion crowns. SIJ and its counterpart, Czech collection units (CIJ) were established in 1993 as subsidiaries of the Finance Ministry and were given loans in order to buy old bad debts for CSOB. They were expected to pay the loans back regardless of their success in recovering bad credit.

- The cabinet decided yesterday that loans and financial aid which were issued at the end of 1995 to certain hospitals due to their inability to pay debts must be paid back. The loans amount to 990 million crowns, of which 440 million was from the government budget and 550 million was represented by credits from Konsolidacni Banka.

- After nearly a year's respite while the cabinet was organising the privatisation of Investicni a Postovni Banka, the cabinet has decided to continue with the sale of more public assets. The cabinet will sell shares of approximately 100 companies amounting to 4.5 billion crowns. PRAVO - The German federal parliament will meet today to discuss and vote on the Czech-German Declaration which was signed on January 21 in Prague by German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus. Representatives will also vote on two proposals for an accompanying document to the declaration. The documents were approved earlier this week by the German coalition and the opposition SPD, but are not supported by CDU and CSU.

- The parliamentary commission for control of the secret service (BIS) did not confirm suspicions of illegal cooperation between the BIS and the Interior Ministry, which Chairman of Parliament and of the Social Democratic Party, Milos Zeman, expressed before presenting the documents. MLADA FRONTA DNES - The Health Ministry conceded yesterday that it shares responsibility for the bad state of General Faculty Hospital, which is deeply indebted to suppliers and is having serious problems obtaining even basic medicines.
- Only eight days after Komercni Banka announced a reduction of certain interest rates, the bank decided on another decrease in rates on some deposits and credits.
